notes: Budgets set by the Technical Director. Re-baselined to measurement after M3 stage 2 (2026-09-29) and again after stage 3 (2026-09-30, 3,000- and 20,000-pass long runs, build/stage3-long/). Units: raster cycles in this spike, DMA included, which is what the runner measures and what adds up to the 19,656-cycle frame (engine/README.md#budget-units). Main-loop routines and zone IRQs get ~5% over the 20,000-pass max, rounded up to 50: the spike's full joint motion cycle is ~88,800 frames (LCM of D's 800, amp's 96 and the X bounces up to 592), so 20,000 is ~22% of it, but the structural worst cases (sort reversal, flicker at minimum D) recur every 800-frame D cycle (25 times in the run), and the maxima moved 0-6% from 3,000 to 20,000 passes. Exact locks only for constant DMA-free paths; mux_irq_top is one again since the stage 3.5 wrap-ghost fix (engine/README.md#wrap-ghosts), locked at 393. The short make test windows won't reach these maxima; the limits must hold in any window. 'stage' is the build stage the engine has reached (docs/milestones/M3-engine-basics.md, rule 1): checks with a higher 'from_stage' print PENDING and fail only under --strict (M3 sign-off). The raster-engineer bumps 'stage' at the start of each stage. Main-loop routines use profile_excl_irq so zone IRQs inside them don't count. Stage 3.5 (2026-09-30, raster-engineer): every check re-measured over 3,000 and 20,000 passes on the new layout; mux_build, both mux_update checks and mux_irq_top re-based (their sources say why), the rest hold with >= 5% over the 20,000-pass max: mux_sort 3,335, mux_select 8,146, mux_irq_zone 2,703, all IRQ time 3,613, mux_max_age 2, late counters 0, spike_idle_min x 16 5,760. Stage 4 (2026-10-01, Technical Director; decision in docs/milestones/M3-engine-basics.md rule 3 and M3-stage4-pinning-diagnosis.md): re-baselined for pinning from a 20,000-pass trace on the stage 4 engine (each check's source has its figures): mux_select 9,400, mux_build 3,100, mux_update 13,000, mux_irq_zone 2,950, all IRQ time 4,000; mux_sort, the fast-path limits and the mux_irq_top lock unchanged. The single free-CPU check (spike_idle_min x 16 >= 5,300 in every frame) is retired: v1's promise is scoped, so there are two checks from stage 4, on labels the spike must provide (engine/README.md#multiplexer-spike-free-cpu-labels): spike_idle_min_normal x 16 >= 5,300 (non-stress frames) and spike_idle_min_stress x 16 >= 4,250 (stress frames). Until the spike has them and 'stage' is 4, both print PENDING and nothing checks free CPU; measured meanwhile: 5,344 and 4,480 over 919,800 frames.

checks.name: free CPU, non-stress frames (the game promise, scoped for v1)
checks.source: docs/milestones/M3-engine-basics.md rule 3, Stage 4 decision (Simon, 2026-10-01): for v1 the promise (>= 7,200 cycles a frame for the game; idle >= 5,300 in the spike, engine/README.md#frame-budget) holds in every frame except a mass sort reversal with pinned sprites in a crowd. A stress frame is one whose spike_move left spike_damp = +1 and spike_amp = 2..5: the four frames in every 48 in which the reversed pattern separates again and the sort re-orders all three groups (engine/README.md#multiplexer-spike-free-cpu-labels). spike_idle_min_normal is the fewest idle iterations in any other frame. The 5,300 is the requirement, unchanged and with no margin of its own. Measured (Technical Director 2026-10-01, stage 4 engine, 4 pinned, frames classified from outside by a checkpoint at spike_main reading the idle count and the motion state): 5,728 over 20,000 frames, 5,344 over 300,000 and over 919,800 (0 frames below 5,300). The two lowest are frames where pinned sprite 1 jumps 219 lines as the player's sweep turns at the top, not sort stress. That long-run margin is 44 cycles (334 iterations against the 332 needed), so the spike's classification code may add at most one iteration (16 cycles) to a frame. With only amp 2..3 counted as stress, two frames in 919,800 (amp 5, D 10: 5,248 and 5,264) fall below, which is why the definition covers the whole re-sort. Idle-loop iterations are 16 cycles (counted) and exclude DMA, so this is conservative. Replaces 'free CPU per frame (game promise)' (spike_idle_min x 16 >= 5,300 in every frame), retired 2026-10-01: with pinning that reads 4,496, the accepted case

checks.name: free CPU, stress frames (v1 floor: sort reversal with pinned sprites in a crowd)
checks.source: The case the Stage 4 decision excludes from the v1 promise, given a floor so a regression still shows. A stress frame is one whose spike_move left spike_damp = +1 and spike_amp = 2..5: the four frames in every 48 in which the reversed pattern separates again and the sort re-orders all three groups (engine/README.md#multiplexer-spike-free-cpu-labels). spike_idle_min_stress is the fewest idle iterations in such a frame. Measured (Technical Director 2026-10-01, same runs as the check above): 4,496 over 20,000 frames (the diagnosis's figure, docs/milestones/M3-stage4-pinning-diagnosis.md), 4,496 over 300,000 and 4,480 over 919,800, where 451 of about 76,650 stress frames are below 5,300 (1 frame in about 2,040 overall). 4,480 - ~5% = 4,256 -> 4,250, rounded down to 50 (rule 7's margin, applied downwards to a minimum). The margin is for run phase and the one iteration the spike's classification code may cost; an engine change that moves the figure is re-baselined, not absorbed. A frame below 5,300 here costs the game nothing unless its own logic needs more than 19,656 - IRQs - mux_update; if it does, the effect is one repeated frame of sprites (mux_update returns C=1), never corruption. Multiplexer v2 must keep 5,300 in these frames too, at which point this check is merged into the one above
